series.title: Building the Batcave
series.description: A multi-agent AI system that lives on Telegram: the architecture, then a post on each agent who lives in it.
series.source_brief: BUILD_IN_PUBLIC.md in the project-batcave repo holds the full editorial briefs (hooks, engineering moments, concrete numbers, persona notes). Read it for grounding before writing any part.

parts.brief: Intro / architecture post for the whole system. The system is a multi-agent AI assistant reachable over Telegram (text, voice, photos). It started Open-Claw-inspired on a GCP Always Free e2-micro running PM2 + Telegram long-polling, which worked until the Claude Agent SDK started spawning child Node processes and the 1 GB box got OOM-killed in a restart loop. The arc to today, told as the real evolution (do NOT describe the dead VM/PM2 stack as current): hand-rolled multi-agent with shared-context handoffs -> Agent SDK query() with isolated subagent contexts + Supabase Postgres for durable state (sessions resume by session_id, survive restarts) -> Cloud Run + webhook + Cloud Tasks, because you cannot run long-polling on a scale-to-zero container and Telegram allows exactly one getUpdates consumer per bot token. The decoupling insight is the spine: an agentic turn takes 10-30s (Whisper -> Haiku router -> Claude Sonnet loop -> ElevenLabs), longer than Telegram's webhook retry window, so the ingest service acks in <100ms, enqueues a Cloud Task, and the worker gets 300s. Idempotency comes free from Cloud Tasks named tasks (update-<update_id> drops Telegram redeliveries). Cost arithmetic: the free e2-micro kept dying, an always-on Cloud Run worker pool was ~$45/mo, webhook + scale-to-zero is ~$0-5/mo; the cost was idle time, not RAM. Introduce the cast the next three posts profile: a Haiku router classifies each message (gordon/ras/alfred/unclear) for ~$0.0003 before anyone sees it; Alfred is the top-level conversational agent; Gordon and Ra's are subagents in isolated contexts. The MCP server is IN-PROCESS via createSdkMcpServer (not a separate external service) and talks to Supabase. Mention the 5-suite eval framework briefly (routing gates PRs, the rest run nightly) but save the depth for later. 'Production-grade' is a banned phrase: show what production actually cost (the OOM kill, the trailing newline in Secret Manager that left the webhook unregistered, the wrong ogg_opus format name that silently killed voice replies). Include one Mermaid diagram of the full request path (Telegram -> ingest -> Cloud Tasks -> worker -> orchestrator -> router/agents -> MCP -> Supabase). This is Part 1 so there is no previous part to link.

Profile Commissioner Gordon, the nutrition agent and the most-built one. Job: track everything you eat - log it, summarize it, set goals, query history, read nutrition labels from photos. He owns 11 MCP tools (search_food, log_food, save_custom_food, daily_summary, recent_history, set_goals, edit_food_entry, delete_food_entry, save_meal, list_saved_meals, log_saved_meal); the first four cover ~90% of use, the rest are corrections and meal templates. The search chain is the best engineering moment: every food search hits a personal custom_foods cache first, then USDA FoodData Central (~600k foods), then Open Food Facts; after logging, the food is upserted to the cache so the next search for the same item skips the API - the cache is built from your own history. Photo recognition has no OCR pipeline and no separate vision model: the Telegram photo arrives as base64, goes straight into the orchestrator prompt as a Claude vision input, and Gordon reads the label or plate directly, names the food, reads macros if visible, asks for serving size if needed, logs it. Meal templates: save_meal stores a named set of items with gram weights, log_saved_meal replays it ('log my usual breakfast'). He remembers goals in nutrition_goals and allergies/preferences in user_facts, loaded at session start. Cost detail: his system prompt embeds a dated macro-goal summary rebuilt once per calendar day, byte-stable within the day, so Anthropic's prompt cache hits every turn after the first. Isolated context: Gordon only ever sees Alfred's task description plus his own system prompt, never the full Alfred thread - explicit context-passing over implicit shared state. SQLite is gone; all state is in Supabase. Persona: warm but authoritative, the detective who wants evidence not excuses, addresses the user as Batman/Bruce. Include one short, real-feeling user<->Gordon exchange that shows the persona and a log action. Include a Mermaid of Gordon's slice (orchestrator -> Gordon subagent -> nutrition MCP tools -> cache/USDA/OFF + Supabase). Roadmap (translate to user-visible capability, no Phase/Sprint labels): smoother barcode-scan flow, smarter goal tuning. Link naturally back to the Part 1 architecture post if it is published.

Profile Alfred, the orchestrator, and be honest that he is the thinnest agent in features - the post is partly about what I want him to become. His actual job today is narrow: routing, general conversation, and user memory. He has exactly three tools: recall_user_facts, store_user_fact, AskUserQuestion. He does not touch food or workout data - 'my AI butler doesn't know anything about food or workouts, he just knows who does.' Engineering moments: (1) The routing problem - letting Alfred pick a specialist via tool_use costs a full Sonnet turn, so a dedicated Haiku router classifies every message before Alfred sees it (one message in, one word out: gordon/ras/alfred/unclear, ~$0.0003, ~700ms). (2) The 'unclear' case - on an ambiguous message the original input is saved to pending_routing in Supabase and Alfred asks which department; the user's clarification is classified and the ORIGINAL message is run through the chosen specialist, so the user never retypes. (3) The defer/resume pattern - AskUserQuestion lets the SDK defer a tool call, the subprocess exits, deferred_state + session_id persist to Supabase, and when the user replies seconds or hours later the orchestrator resumes and resolves it; sessions with a pending question never expire. (4) The wrong optimization - sticky routing (skip the Haiku call for 5 minutes after a turn) was added and immediately broke domain switching (after Alfred said 'no emails' you couldn't log food for 5 minutes); it was removed. The router costs $0.0003, run it every turn. Persona: Alfred Pennyworth, dry Michael Caine butler, says 'Sir', never alarmed; the voice is an ElevenLabs clone (the voice is literally named 'George' but sounds like Caine so it stays). Include one short real-feeling exchange in voice. The honest framing: Alfred is the front door and the memory, but the genuinely useful butler stuff isn't built yet - what I want next, as user-visible capability: check my calendar and email, and tell me when the wind looks good for kiting. Include a Mermaid of the routing/defer path (message -> Haiku router -> Alfred or specialist; unclear -> clarify -> rerun original). Link naturally back to the architecture post and/or Gordon if published.

Profile Ra's al Ghul, the workout agent and the simplest one by design. Job: log workout sets, query workout history, remember training context. Nothing else. Four tools: log_workout_set (exercise, sets, reps, weight, optional notes), workout_history (queryable by exercise over a date range), recall_user_facts, store_user_fact. The log_workout_set flow: 'I squatted 100kg for 5 sets of 3' becomes structured rows in workout_log, one row per set, so later you can ask 'what was my squat last week' and get exact numbers, not a narrative. The sharpest point is the contrast with Gordon: Gordon is warm and explains; Ra's is terse and logs and moves on - and that terseness is a deliberate design constraint, not flavor. If Ra's started explaining periodization, users would chat with him instead of logging, and the data would get messy; the agent stays focused so the data stays clean. Same isolation pattern as Gordon: fresh context per invocation, Alfred delegates a task description ('log a 5x3 squat at 100kg'), Ra's never sees the prior conversation. User facts double as training context - Ra's can store training schedule / injury history / current program and recall them, which is how he 'knows' you do CrossFit without Alfred re-explaining each time. Persona: terse, disciplined, performance over comfort, addresses the user as Detective/Bruce, ElevenLabs cloned voice; no 'good job', just the log. Include one short real-feeling exchange that shows exactly how little he says. Honest roadmap (user-visible, no Phase labels): progression and PR tracking, maybe lightweight programming later - but the whole point is he's a clean log first. Include a Mermaid of Ra's slice (orchestrator -> Ra's subagent -> workout MCP tools -> Supabase workout_log). Link naturally back to an earlier published part.
